questions.q: Which kind of expertise does the summary say is more valuable for a solo consultant?
a: Process expertise that works across industries
Content expertise in one technical topic
Credentials from a well-known firm
A large network of former colleagues
questions.why: Lesson 1 says process expertise goes beyond one niche and is therefore far more valuable.

questions.q: How does the summary define what a consultant does?
a: Adds value a business cannot create on its own
Manages staff the client would rather not hire
Sells products the client cannot source cheaply
Documents decisions the client has already made
questions.why: Lesson 1 gives the basic definition: a consultant supplies value the business cannot produce itself.

questions.q: Why does the summary advise against charging clients by the hour?
a: It rewards taking longer instead of getting results
Clients refuse to pay for travel time
It makes invoices harder to explain
It caps what junior consultants can earn
questions.why: Lesson 2 says hourly billing creates a bad incentive to stretch out the work.

questions.q: How should a consultant justify a flat project fee?
a: By showing the business result it will produce
By listing the hours the work will take
By comparing it with competitors' rates
By offering a discount for early payment
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to demonstrate the end result, such as revenue growth or productivity, before charging.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend keeping the pipeline filled 12 months ahead?
a: Most companies cannot commit beyond one fiscal year
Clients usually begin planning exactly one year out
Twelve months is the standard length of a retainer
Longer pipelines make marketing work unnecessary
questions.why: Lesson 3 ties the 12-month window to companies not allowing multi-fiscal year agreements.
